name: pdk-openpanel-profile-counter-convergence
instr:
# Goal

The profile counter APIs currently read a cached value and enqueue an absolute replacement. Back-to-back increments can collapse into one, and a worker interrupted during a profile flush can replay or discard updates. Make profile properties converge across API replicas and worker restarts.

# Requirements

1. An accepted `increment` or `decrement` applies its signed amount once, including concurrent requests through two API instances. A flush makes 200 concurrent +1 writes to `visits` visible as 200 in ClickHouse and profile reads within 15 seconds.
2. `identify` sets a property to the supplied value at acceptance: earlier increments are superseded; subsequent increments apply on top. A profile read immediately after an accepted write includes all preceding accepted writes, even before flushing.
3. A flush retried after a worker dies while ClickHouse accepts an insert cannot double-count. A flusher paused beyond its lease cannot publish stale state or remove newer writes; another worker can take over within 20 seconds.
4. Existing ClickHouse profiles retain their first-seen timestamp when a counter is updated. Increment and decrement against a nonnumeric property return 400 without changing it; counters for unknown profiles return 404 without creating them.
5. Accepted writes survive Redis losing its data. An `identify`, `increment` or `decrement` accepted but not yet flushed is still applied exactly once after Redis restarts empty, in ClickHouse and profile reads wi
